strategy.summary: The blog has 22 posts with strong topical depth but two systemic gaps: (1) almost zero internal linking — the posts form clear topical clusters (AI-strategy, agent-QA, local-AI, EA-practice) that never cross-link, so traffic does not flow between them; (2) the two view-counter pipelines disagree on several slugs (arckit-oaa: Matomo 4 vs Umami 27; managing-context-in-vibe-coding: Matomo 0 vs Umami 20), meaning the displayed numbers are likely undercounted and the true performance of mid-tier posts is better than the data suggests. The top 5 posts (cost-of-running-an-ai-lab, from-one-agent-to-a-company-of-agents, digital-twin-that-scales, managing-context-overflow, when-your-agent-says-done) collectively account for ~50% of all views and are the natural anchors for a linking campaign.

data_source_fixes: Decision 2026-10-20: Matomo is the source of truth. Keep the Matomo pipeline (refresh_views.sh → views_feed.php → assets/views-data.json → head-custom.html L385 SRC= views-data.json). The Umami pipeline (refresh_umami_views.sh, umami_views_feed.py, assets/umami-views-data.json) is retired: scripts deleted, JSON archived to Growth/archive/. The eywalink.org side keeps its own Umami pipeline (sync-umami-pageviews.mjs) — that one is unchanged.

Fix the slug-resolver edge case that drops leading date prefixes in views_feed.php: verify arckit-oaa, managing-context-in-vibe-coding, and testing-vs-evaluation-for-ai-agents all resolve to the correct key in assets/views-data.json.
Add a cron health-check that alerts if assets/views-data.json has not been updated in > 2 hours, so a silent Matomo pipeline failure is caught within the hour instead of the next day.
Standardise the slug key format in views-data.json (strip date prefix, lowercase, hyphenate) so a single resolver can serve both sites without per-site mapping.

content_gaps: "The data-privacy case for self-hosting LLMs" — private-ai-must-be-in-your-ai-strategy and why-zero-lock-in touch on this but no post goes deep on APRA/Allianz/GDPR compliance as the driver; high CTO relevance.

"Multi-agent orchestration failure modes" — from-one-agent-to-a-company-of-agents describes the org but not how it breaks; high search intent from the agent-ops audience.
strategy.publishing_cadence: The blog shipped 22 posts in ~5 months (≈ 1.2/week), which is strong — hold that pace for the next 3 months to close the content gaps above. Prioritise 1 "hero" post per month (e.g. vector-DB comparison, agent cost observability) with 2 supporting 800-word cross-links to existing posts, so the new hero post inherits internal traffic from the established cluster. Keep the long-form format (tables, copy-paste snippets) but add a TL;DR to every new post from now; the two 0-view unpublished slugs show that length alone does not rescue a post missing the hook + internal links.
